Interface Journal<T>

Type Parameters:
T - the entry payload type
All Known Implementing Classes:
DefaultJournal
public interface Journal<T>
A distributed append-only event stream with per-entry TTLs, a completion lifecycle, and monotonic ordering.

Each journal is identified by a unique key and supports multiple concurrent producers and consumers. Entries are appended with individual time-to-live durations and are assigned monotonically increasing IDs that can be used as resume checkpoints.

Inactivity TTL. A journal is created with an inactivity TTL (see JournalFactory.create(String, Class, Duration)). If no entries are appended within that duration the journal auto-expires and subsequent operations throw JournalExpiredException. Each successful append resets the inactivity timer.

Completion and retention. Calling complete(Duration) marks the journal as completed. No further appends are accepted (they throw JournalCompletedException), but existing entries remain readable for the specified retention period. Once the retention TTL elapses the journal expires fully.

All methods are thread-safe.

Usage example

// Producer
Journal<String> journal = factory.create("events", String.class, Duration.ofMinutes(30));
journal.append("event-1", Duration.ofHours(1));
journal.append("event-2", Duration.ofHours(1));
journal.complete(Duration.ofMinutes(5));

// Consumer
BlockingSubscription<JournalEntry<String>> sub = journal.subscribe();
while (sub.isActive()) {
    NextResult<JournalEntry<String>> result = sub.next(Duration.ofSeconds(5));
    switch (result) {
        case NextResult.Value<JournalEntry<String>> v -> process(v.value());
        case NextResult.Timeout<?> t -> { /* poll again *​/ }
        case NextResult.Completed<?> c -> log.info("journal completed");
        case NextResult.Expired<?> e -> log.warn("journal expired");
        case NextResult.Deleted<?> d -> log.warn("journal deleted");
        case NextResult.Errored<?> err -> log.error("error", err.cause());
    }
}

  • Method Details

    • append

      String append(T data, Duration ttl)
      Appends an entry to this journal with the given time-to-live.

      Each successful append resets the journal's inactivity timer.

      The entry TTL is a per-record retention hint rather than a lease, so Duration.ZERO is legal and means "store this entry without a TTL". Backends that manage retention at the stream level rather than per entry ignore the value entirely.

      Parameters:
      data - the entry payload
      ttl - time-to-live for this individual entry, or Duration.ZERO for no TTL
      Returns:
      the generated entry ID, monotonically ordered with respect to other entries in this journal
      Throws:
      JournalCompletedException - if this journal has already been completed
      JournalExpiredException - if this journal has expired or been deleted
      IllegalArgumentException - if ttl is negative or exceeds the maximum allowed entry TTL

    • complete

      void complete(Duration retentionTtl)
      Marks this journal as completed with the given retention TTL.

      After completion no further entries may be appended. Existing entries and active subscriptions remain readable until the retention period elapses, at which point the journal expires fully.

      Like the entry TTL, the retention TTL is a retention hint rather than a lease: Duration.ZERO is legal and means "retain without a TTL".

      Parameters:
      retentionTtl - how long the journal remains readable after completion, or Duration.ZERO for no TTL
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if retentionTtl is negative or exceeds the maximum allowed retention TTL

    • delete

      void delete()
      Explicitly deletes this journal and all of its entries.

      Active subscriptions receive a NextResult.Deleted result.

    • subscribe

      BlockingSubscription<JournalEntry<T>> subscribe()
      Subscribe from the current tail. Only entries appended after this call are delivered. Historical entries (those already in the journal when subscribe is called) are NOT replayed.
      Returns:
      a blocking subscription that delivers future entries

    • subscribeAfter

      BlockingSubscription<JournalEntry<T>> subscribeAfter(String afterId)
      Subscribe starting strictly after afterId. All entries with an id greater than afterId are delivered, followed by new entries as they arrive. Useful for resuming from a persisted checkpoint.
      Parameters:
      afterId - the entry ID to resume after (exclusive)
      Returns:
      a blocking subscription starting after the given entry

    • subscribeLast

      BlockingSubscription<JournalEntry<T>> subscribeLast(int count)
      Subscribe starting with the last count retained entries, then continue with new entries as they arrive. Useful for "show the last N events, then tail" patterns.
      Parameters:
      count - the number of recent entries to replay before tailing
      Returns:
      a blocking subscription starting from the last count entries
